source.edition: Elementary Topology, Michael C. Gemignani, Second Edition
source.visualReview: Full supplied PDF pages141,142,146 and149 visually inspected. Adjacent mathematical prose was consulted on PDF140,145,147,148 and150; all three native SVGs were inspected beside source crops.
source.boundsConvention: sourceBounds is normalized [x,y,width,height] against the full PDF page, including graphic and labels while excluding prose and captions.

implementation.semantics: Reusable open-cover/subfamily, compactness, Lindelof, separated-subset/ball-family, Hausdorff-pair and finite-cover reach declarations. Substance snapshots store mathematical facts with no shape or pixel data.
implementation.styleReuse: Three covering-property policies share topologyDrawing, native equations, vector hatch policy and colors. Compact intersections use nested native masks, and the separated-set display remains independent of metric data.
implementation.graphics: Native Penrose circle/line/path/equation/group shapes; no raster wrappers.
implementation.interactive: All build factories accept final optional FigureRenderOptions and forward variation/interactive after canonical defaults.

verification.visualReview: All three optimized SVGs rasterized on white backgrounds and inspected beside source crops. The source u dot and selected cross hatches were restored after comparison.
verification.scope: Strict metric ball separation, finite-cover extension arithmetic, contradiction hypotheses, generic compactness premises, finite pair/cover relations and actual rendered contour membership are checked. Universal proofs and pixel identity are not claimed.

figures.sourceContext: Proposition 5, Lindelof implies separable in a metric space. Its argument starts on supplied printed 148 and continues on supplied printed 149: take a maximal subset E with D(a,b)>=p for distinct a,b, let V be the complement of the union of Cl N(a,p/4), and cover X by V and all N(a,p/2). Each center forces its own covering half-ball to remain, so Lindelof makes E countable.
geometry: The original three-by-three array of hatched closed quarter-ball representations with nine black center marks.
Original V, Cl N(a,p/4) and central a labels. No additional outer half-ball outlines are introduced.
facts: Generic MaximalSeparatedSubset with positive separation p, SeparatedIn(E,X,tau), Lindelof(tau) and the Countable(E) conclusion.
MetricBallFamily radii p/4 and p/2; ClosuresOfFamily for quarter balls; UnionOf(K,closedQuarterFamily), ClosedIn(K,tau), and ComplementOf(V,K,X).
The open cover contains V and the complete half-ball family. IndispensableCenteredCover records the reason every center requires its own half-ball.
checks: Numeric radii reject nonpositive, nonfinite and underflowed data. Strict half-balls at separation p cannot overlap, including the tangent midpoint.
The immutable snapshot has no finite point array or coordinate points for E.
Actual native SVG has nine illustrative disk fills and nine point markers; no added half-ball outlines or raster images.
limits: The displayed grid is a finite schematic prefix of generic E and does not assert that E is finite or a lattice.
The scan does not use one numerical metric scale for both center spacing and p/4 disk radii. Pixel positions stay in Style and do not become mathematical distances.
The circles illustrate closures of generic metric neighborhoods; they do not assert that closures equal closed metric balls in every metric space.

figures.sourceContext: Proposition 7, Case 1 of compactness of [0,1]: T contains the x whose [0,x) have a finite subcover. Assuming interior proposed supremum u belongs to T, add a cover element U_i prime containing u. Openness then extends finite cover reach beyond u, contradicting the upper-bound hypothesis. The definition and Case 1 begin on supplied printed 152.
geometry: Original real axis with marked 0, u and 1, one hatched open interval around u and its round open-end marks.
Original U_i prime and u labels; the mathematical extension witness v is kept invisible, matching the original graphic.
facts: Default u=0.55 and chosen witness interval (0.40,0.72), with a genuine finite prefix covering [0,u).
The enlarged finite subfamily covers [0,v], where v=(u+min(b,1))/2>u, and Member(v,T) supplies the contradiction witness.
checks: For several interior u and local intervals the computed v is strictly larger, inside the witness interval and inside [0,1].
Invalid boundary u and intervals not containing u are rejected.
Both finite subcover relations and the proposed supremum hypothesis are retained; no true SupremumOf assertion is made.
Actual SVG retains all three source point dots, the open interval marks and no visible v annotation.
limits: This is the illustrated Case 1; the source Case 2 and full compactness proof remain in the supplied prose.
The chosen numeric interval is a valid realization of the generic cover member, not a specific interval supplied by the book.

figures.sourceContext: Proposition 11 and its supplied proof opening state that a compact subset A of a T2 space is closed. The outside x must have a neighborhood avoiding A. The printed continuation page 157 is missing. The visible graphic names paired V_y and U_y neighborhoods, their cover union V and the intersection U.
geometry: Two source panels retained within one framed native SVG: overlapping neighborhoods around hatched compact A, and a separate common neighborhood around the marked outside x.
Original A, V, V_y1, V_yn, y1, yn, U, U_y1, U_yn and x labels and their white knockouts.
The two named cover neighborhoods use crossing hatching. Four nested native clip masks produce a true common hatch intersection of the depicted outside neighborhood contours.
facts: CompactIn(A,tau) and T2(tau), with A initially a generic Set rather than a ClosedSet, avoiding the conclusion as a premise.
Six illustrative HausdorffNeighborhoodPair witnesses, a finite open subcover of A and the matched finite outside-neighborhood family.
FiniteIntersectionOf(U,outsideFamily), UnionOf(V,finiteCover), Member(x,U), Subset(A,V) and Disjoint(U,V).
checks: Every paired U,V is open, contains its named point and is disjoint; every selected V belongs to the finite cover, and every U contains the final intersection.
The style rejects incomplete Hausdorff witness programs.
Actual rendered cubic contours contain their named selected y points and contain x in every depicted outside neighborhood.
Native nested clipping, three point markers, original labels and absence of image elements are checked.
figures.missingProse: Printed page 157 is absent from the supplied PDF. The union/intersection construction in this Substance program is the standard consequence of the supplied proposition and named diagram, not a transcription of the missing proof wording.
limits: Smooth contours approximate the scanned irregular boundaries. Hatch density is lighter, with the consistent subdued orange fill.

The finite family and n labels are schematic: six chosen witnesses illustrate the compact subcover, and the right panel shows representative neighborhood contours rather than asserting the count of distinct sets from line loops.
The unseen proof continuation has not been reconstructed as book prose.
